answer: A registry can require every agent to lock a ferrous-hard stake that is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicate identities. One honest agent is cheap to register, but spawning thousands of fakes means locking capital behind each one, so the attacker's cost scales linearly with the fraud. The stake also leaves a pigment-like trace: reused funding sources and identical behaviour mark clones, and one detection can ripple through the whole cluster, burning every linked deposit at once. Farming fake identities then costs more than it can ever earn.
